original_question: Determine whether the anomalous phenomenon called redshift quantization, introduced by Tifft, should be generalized to other astrophysical phenomena, whether it implies quantized distances between galaxies, whether such quantized distances would in turn imply quantized vortices or cosmic-string-like structure on astrophysical scales, and what other observations support or refute that picture.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2.10, "Does Tifft’s redshift quantization imply quantized distance between galaxies?" The draft is targeting the four linked bullet questions in that subsection, not a broader neighboring problem. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft already captures the subsection’s main chain of questions: Tifft’s redshift quantization, whether it implies quantized distances between galaxies, whether that would suggest quantized vortices or cosmic-string-like structure on astrophysical scales, and what further observations might support or refute that picture. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
missing_details: The official scope is subsection-level and narrower than a general theory of macroquantization: §3.2.10 is specifically organized around Tifft’s redshift quantization and its possible implication for intergalactic distance quantization. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The draft omits the paper’s basic variables and definitions: redshift z, distance r, Hubble constant H, and the speed of light c, together with the Hubble-law relation z = Hr/c. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

It also omits the paper’s explicit modeling assumption that the major part of the redshift can be treated as Doppler, so z = v/c for recession velocity v. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The specific empirical input used in the subsection is Tifft’s reported discrete velocities 36.6 km/s and 72.2 km/s; the draft mentions quantization but not these values. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The paper’s proposed distance quantization is stated in formula form: δr = (c/H)δz and r_n = r_0 + nδr, with n = 1, 2, 3, ... and r_0 a baseline distance. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
A key scope restriction is missing: the text says the implication is quantized distance between galaxies in the same cluster. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The vortex interpretation is not merely metaphorical in the paper; it is tied to the quantization condition ∮ p·dr = Nh and to Gross-Pitaevskii/topological-vortex language. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

To make the question paper-faithful, the 'other observations' should be those actually invoked nearby: CMB-spectrum fits and galaxy rotation curves from Moffat’s quantum-phion-condensate model, plus Fundamental Plane cluster and quasar redshift data compared with equations (6) and (7). ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here, because this target is an astrophysical open problem rather than an algebraic conjecture. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
refined_question: Assuming the standard Hubble relation z = Hr/c and, as in §3.2.10, that the dominant part of the observed redshift is Doppler so that z = v/c, do Tifft’s reported discrete redshift/velocity increments (36.6 km/s and 72.2 km/s) imply, for galaxies in the same cluster, a quantized distance law δr = (c/H)δz and hence r_n = r_0 + nδr for integers n = 1, 2, 3, ...; and, if so, can this quantized-distance picture be extended to other astrophysical phenomena by interpreting it as evidence for astrophysical topologically quantized vortices satisfying ∮ p·dr = Nh, in the Gross-Pitaevskii / quantum-phion-condensate picture and by analogy with cosmic strings, with the nearby cited observations (CMB-spectrum fits, galaxy rotation curves, Fundamental Plane clusters, and quasar redshift data) used to assess support for or against that interpretation? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under z = Hr/c, ask whether Tifft’s quantized-redshift data give a redshift ladder z_n = z_0 + nδz that is equivalent to the distance ladder r_n = r_0 + nδr, with δr = (c/H)δz. The paper explicitly presents this as an equivalent reformulation of the quantized-distance proposal. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper: it essentially paraphrases the four bullet questions listed in §3.2.10. The rewrite therefore stays centered on that subsection rather than broadening the problem to the book’s more general macroquantization discussion. What needed sharpening was not the thematic direction, but the hidden setup: the Hubble-law and Doppler assumptions, the specific discrete velocities used, the same-cluster restriction, the exact quantized-distance law r_n = r_0 + nδr, and the fact that the vortex interpretation is framed through the quantization condition ∮ p·dr = Nh and the Gross-Pitaevskii/topological-vortex picture. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
